summary_text: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 0.84% (Movilh regional table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year. There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression since the return of democracy. Protective national framework (Gender Identity Law 21.120 in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, anti-discrimination law 21.220) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (PAIG excluded from the 2026 budget; health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors; legislative initiative CEI-57) and administrative document friction from Registro Civil identification-system issuance failures (Comptroller Final Report 264/2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.

sources.title: Chile | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Chile (updated March 2026): same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; hate-crime law aggravating SOGI motives since 2012; civil unions since 2015; self-determined legal gender recognition since 2019; third-sex birth option for intersex children since 2006; no statutory ban on medically unnecessary intersex surgeries (2023 health-ministry guidance is non-binding); the country's first lesbophobic-femicide conviction (2025, penal code art. 390 ter, which aggravates killings motivated by sexual orientation/gender identity/expression); broad positive societal opinion but trans-rights pushback echoing the UK Cass Report — a 2024 parliamentary commission on trans minors reported in May 2025 recommending a ban on hormonal treatment for minors and audits of gender-affirming programmes; the Gender Identity Support Programme (PAIG) was excluded from the 2026 budget; concern over the 2025 presidential victory of a member of an anti-marriage-equality political network.

sources.title: 2024 was ‘year of regression’ for LGBTQ rights in Chile
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: extraction returned only site navigation at fetch time (article body not retrievable); headline of record: '2024 was year of regression for LGBTQ rights in Chile' — national-level regression context, no region-specific content.

Movilh XXIV Annual Human Rights Report on sexual and gender diversity in Chile (facts 2025, published March 2026): the national annual history of LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases, including the per-region case-share table used here and national totals — 3,620 recorded cases in 2025 (+27.1%, highest on record; 23% of all cases in 24 years), 2,847 in 2024 (+78.7%, the first regression since the return of democracy) — plus the 2025-26 national rollback (PAIG removed from the 2026 budget, health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors, legislative initiative CEI-57 against trans children's rights).
